news.title: Premier League joins top European leagues in call for reforms to way Fifa is run
news.lede: The 2026 World Cup was hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico. The Premier League has joined three of its top European counterparts in calling for "fundamental" reform of the way that Fifa is run, claiming its president Gianni Infantino has "actively promoted exploitative ideas". In a joint statement with Spain's La Liga, Germany's Bundesliga, and Italy's Serie A, the English top flight says it is speaking out "because we understand how Fifa's relentless expansionism affects everyone". The four leagues say the shake-up is needed to make world football's governing body "transparent, objective, proportionate and inclusive" and claim that "our sport cannot grow globally if its foundations are undermined".

news.title: Emile Heskey makes coaching prediction after England's World Cup third place
news.lede: England legend Emile Heskey has hailed the impact of England’s World Cup performances this summer on the next generation of football coaches. The former international striker-turned-coach made the trip to St George’s Park to reflect on how an inspirational showing at a major international tournament can encourage football coaching as a viable career pathway. New research from YouGov has revealed the wider impact of this summer’s tournament, with the feel-good factor motivating a new generation to get involved in the game. More than half of England fans (57%) say the tournament left them with a more positive perception of the England National Team, whilst almost three quarters (73%) say it made them feel proud of the side.

news.title: David Beckham takes £39m dividend as World Cup deals drive record profits
news.lede: Former footballer appeared in about 12 ad campaigns this summer, pushing holding company’s revenue to $110.5m. David Beckham has taken a $51m (£39m) dividend from his business empire after a series of deals with brands for the Fifa World Cup. Beckham appeared in about a dozen ad campaigns across this summer’s tournament in the US, working with brands including Lenovo, McDonald’s, Bank of America, Verizon and the PepsiCo crisps brand Lay’s. The World Cup work helped to fuel a record year for DRJB Holdings, the commercial company for Beckham’s brands business, where revenues surged by a fifth to $110.5m last year, up from $92.3m in 2024.
